conclusion: With only the loss weights changed (none -> 2**(-age/10), mean one), the seed-mean paired daily all-eight-time RankIC difference against the retained 10-day/1500 reference was +0.010851 against the unchanged floor of 0.011647; per window research_a: +0.027178, research_b: -0.005476. The direct contrast against the equal-weight 40-day/6000 arm was -0.009578 (research_a: -0.013318, research_b: -0.005838). The candidate fails the predeclared gates both_windows_improve, minimum_mean_gain, worst_day_guardrail, so the 10-day reference is retained. The three seed results are complete; this is not evidence that every recency half-life or step count is uninformative.

hypothesis: The 40-day pool failed its worst-day guardrail because old dates diluted the recent regime. Fixed exponential recency weights with a ten-trading-day half-life should keep the 40-day sample but restore the recent-date emphasis, clearing the unchanged promotion gates against the 10-day/1500 reference.
limitations: Two research windows and three seeds are selection data, not independent confirmation.
The ten-day half-life is this project's predeclared choice; no other half-life was searched.
The equal-weight control isolates the weighting effect but was trained in the prior round; its source snapshot differs only in the loss-weighting code path.
6000 steps is 0.60 epochs of the 40-day pool; heavier schedules are outside this round.
Local gross metrics exclude fees and slippage; platform time and memory limits remain unverified.
next_steps: If accepted, run a separately frozen confirmation on untouched dates before any platform claim.
If rejected, report the weighting effect against the equal-weight control before proposing another half-life; this round deliberately tested only 10 days.
